eras.title: The world after Napoleon
eras.summary: Napoleon is gone and Vienna has redrawn Europe. Britain rules the seas, and Spain’s American empire is beginning to crack.

assign.GR~ionian: GB_EMPIRE|United States of the Ionian Islands

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase
events.detail: France sold its vast Louisiana territory to the United States, roughly doubling the young country and carrying it west to the Rocky Mountains.

events.title: Río de la Plata breaks away
events.detail: Buenos Aires deposed the Spanish viceroy in 1810, and Paraguay and Artigas’s Banda Oriental went their own ways. Elsewhere, royalists had the upper hand again by 1815.

events.title: Sweden loses Finland, gains Norway
events.detail: Russia took Finland from Sweden in 1809. In 1814 Denmark, on the losing side, gave Norway to Sweden; Norway kept its own constitution and parliament under the Swedish king.

events.title: Britain keeps the Cape
events.detail: By the 1814 peace, Britain kept the Cape and Demerara from the Dutch, and Mauritius, the Seychelles, Tobago and St Lucia from France. Malta stayed British too.

events.title: The Congress of Vienna
events.detail: Europe’s powers redrew the map at Vienna, signing days before Waterloo. A German Confederation of 39 states took the place of the Holy Roman Empire, and Austria gained Lombardy–Venetia.

events.title: Prussia reaches the Rhine
events.detail: Prussia gained the Rhineland, Westphalia and the northern half of Saxony, stretching the kingdom across northern Germany from the Memel to the Saar.

events.title: A united Netherlands
events.detail: The former Austrian Netherlands were joined to the Dutch provinces as a single kingdom under William I, a buffer against France. He also became Grand Duke of Luxembourg.

events.title: Congress Poland
events.detail: Napoleon’s Duchy of Warsaw was divided again. Its heart became the Kingdom of Poland, with the Russian tsar as king, while Prussia took back Posen and Kraków became a free city.

eras.title: Nations unite
eras.summary: Germany and Italy are newly united, Austria-Hungary is a dual monarchy, and much of inner Africa still lies beyond Europe’s empires.

events.title: Latin America breaks free
events.detail: Between 1810 and 1825 Spain loses its mainland American empire, the last great battle coming at Ayacucho in 1824. Brazil leaves Portugal in 1822.

events.title: France conquers Algeria
events.detail: French troops take Algiers in 1830, ending Ottoman rule there. The conquest of the north takes decades, and in 1848 Algeria is declared part of France.

events.title: The US reaches the Pacific
events.detail: Spain cedes Florida in 1819, Texas joins in 1845 and Oregon follows in 1846. Mexico cedes the Southwest in 1848, and Russia sells Alaska in 1867.

events.title: Canada is born
events.detail: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick unite as the Dominion of Canada. It takes over Rupert’s Land in 1870, and British Columbia joins in 1871.

events.title: Russia expands across Asia
events.detail: Russia takes Outer Manchuria from China in 1858–60 and founds Vladivostok. In Central Asia it takes Tashkent and Samarkand and makes Bukhara a protectorate.

events.title: Rome completes Italy
events.detail: Italian troops enter Rome in September 1870, ending the Papal States. Most of the peninsula had united in 1859–61, and Venice joined in 1866.

events.title: Germany unites
events.detail: Prussia’s North German Confederation and the southern states of Bavaria, Württemberg, Baden and Hesse form the German Empire, proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871.

events.title: France loses Alsace-Lorraine
events.detail: Defeated in the Franco-Prussian War, France cedes Alsace and part of Lorraine to Germany by the Treaty of Frankfurt in May 1871.

eras.title: The eve of the Great War
eras.summary: Europe’s empires rule most of the world, Africa is almost entirely partitioned, and a new republic replaces China’s last dynasty.

events.title: The Congress of Berlin
events.detail: Serbia, Montenegro and Romania win full independence and Bulgaria gains autonomy. Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia, then annexes it in 1908.

events.title: The Scramble for Africa
events.detail: European powers carve up almost the whole continent within thirty years. Only Ethiopia, which defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896, and Liberia stay independent.

events.title: The Spanish–American War
events.detail: After a short war in 1898, the United States takes the Philippines, Puerto Rico and Guam from Spain, which sells its other Pacific islands to Germany. Cuba becomes independent in 1902.

events.title: South Africa unites
events.detail: Britain conquers the Boer republics of the Transvaal and Orange Free State in 1899–1902. In 1910 they join the Cape and Natal as the Union of South Africa.

events.title: Japan annexes Korea
events.detail: Japan, which took Taiwan in 1895 and southern Sakhalin in 1905, formally annexes Korea as Chōsen.

events.title: Italy takes Libya
events.detail: Italy seizes Tripolitania and Cyrenaica from the Ottoman Empire in the Italo-Turkish War of 1911–12.

events.title: China becomes a republic
events.detail: The Qing dynasty falls after more than 260 years and the Republic of China is proclaimed. Mongolia and Tibet break away and govern themselves.

events.title: The Balkan Wars
events.detail: The Ottomans lose nearly all their European lands. Serbia, Greece, Montenegro and Bulgaria grow, Romania takes Southern Dobruja from Bulgaria, and Albania is born as a new state.

eras.title: Empires fall
eras.summary: Four empires have fallen. New states fill eastern Europe, and the victors govern Germany’s colonies and Ottoman lands as mandates.

events.title: New nations from Finland to Poland
events.detail: As the Russian and German empires collapsed, Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania won independence, and Poland returned after 123 years of partition.

events.title: Austria-Hungary breaks apart
events.detail: The Habsburg empire split into Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia and a new South Slav kingdom, while Poland, Romania and Italy took in its other lands.

events.title: Germany’s colonies change hands
events.detail: The Treaty of Versailles took Germany’s colonies away. The League of Nations gave them to the victors to govern as mandates, from Tanganyika to the Pacific islands.

events.title: Versailles redraws Germany
events.detail: The Treaty of Versailles returned Alsace-Lorraine to France and gave Poland Posen and West Prussia, a corridor to the Baltic. Danzig became a free city.

events.title: The Middle East is divided
events.detail: At San Remo the Allies shared out the Ottoman Arab lands as mandates: Syria and Lebanon went to France, and Iraq, Palestine and Transjordan to Britain.

events.title: The Irish Free State
events.detail: Under the Anglo-Irish Treaty, 26 counties became the self-governing Irish Free State in December 1922. Northern Ireland stayed in the United Kingdom.

events.title: The Soviet Union is founded
events.detail: After the 1917 revolution and a long civil war, Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia joined together as the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics in December 1922.

events.title: The Republic of Turkey
events.detail: The Treaty of Lausanne in July 1923 settled Turkey’s borders after the Ottoman defeat. In October, Mustafa Kemal proclaimed the republic, with Ankara as its capital.

eras.title: On the brink of war
eras.summary: Germany and Italy have annexed their neighbours, Japan rules Manchuria, and Europe’s empires still span much of the globe.

events.title: Japan sets up Manchukuo
events.detail: After seizing Manchuria in 1931, Japan proclaimed the state of Manchukuo, with Puyi, the last Qing emperor, as its figurehead ruler.

events.title: Saudi Arabia is proclaimed
events.detail: Ibn Saud, ruler of Nejd, conquered the Hejaz in 1925 and in 1932 united his lands as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Iraq becomes independent
events.detail: The British mandate ended and the Kingdom of Iraq joined the League of Nations, though Britain kept air bases and a strong influence.

events.title: Italy conquers Ethiopia
events.detail: Italian forces took Addis Ababa in May 1936. Ethiopia was joined with Eritrea and Italian Somaliland as Italian East Africa.

events.title: Germany annexes Austria
events.detail: In March 1938 German troops crossed into Austria, which was absorbed into the Reich and renamed the Ostmark.

events.title: Czechoslovakia is broken up
events.detail: Germany took the Sudetenland in 1938 and Bohemia and Moravia in March 1939. Slovakia became a German client state and Hungary seized Carpatho-Ukraine.

events.title: Italy invades Albania
events.detail: Italian troops landed in Albania in April 1939. King Zog fled, and the Albanian crown passed to the King of Italy.

events.title: Franco wins in Spain
events.detail: Spain became a republic in 1931. The civil war that began in 1936 ended in April 1939 with victory for Franco’s Nationalists, and he ruled as dictator.

eras.title: A world divided
eras.summary: The Iron Curtain splits Europe and Germany, while India, Pakistan, Indonesia and other new Asian states step out of the old empires.

events.title: Italy loses its African empire
events.detail: British and Ethiopian forces freed Ethiopia in 1941 and Haile Selassie returned. Libya, Eritrea and Italian Somaliland passed to British administration.

events.title: Borders move west
events.detail: The USSR annexed the Baltic states, eastern Poland and northern East Prussia. Poland was shifted west onto German lands up to the Oder and Neisse.

events.title: Britain leaves South Asia
events.detail: British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan in August 1947, uprooting millions. Burma and Ceylon became independent in early 1948.

events.title: Israel is founded
events.detail: Israel declared independence as the British mandate in Palestine ended in May 1948. After the war, Jordan held the West Bank and Egypt the Gaza Strip.

events.title: Korea is divided
events.detail: Freed from Japanese rule in 1945 and split at the 38th parallel, Korea became two states in 1948: the Republic of Korea and the DPRK.

events.title: Two German states
events.detail: The western occupation zones became the Federal Republic in May 1949 and the Soviet zone the German Democratic Republic in October. Berlin was split too.

events.title: People’s Republic of China
events.detail: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People’s Republic of China on 1 October 1949. The Nationalist government withdrew to Taiwan.

events.title: Indonesia gains independence
events.detail: After four years of struggle, the Netherlands handed sovereignty to the United States of Indonesia in December 1949. Western New Guinea stayed Dutch.

eras.title: The Year of Africa
eras.summary: Seventeen African nations win independence in 1960, while Europe stays split between East and West.

events.title: China takes control of Tibet
events.detail: Chinese troops entered Tibet in 1950 and Lhasa in 1951. After a failed uprising in 1959, the Dalai Lama fled into exile in India.

events.title: French Indochina breaks up
events.detail: Cambodia and Laos won independence in 1953. After France’s defeat at Dien Bien Phu, the 1954 Geneva Accords split Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

events.title: Independence in North Africa
events.detail: Libya became an independent kingdom in 1951. Sudan, Morocco and Tunisia followed in 1956, as Britain, Egypt, France and Spain gave up control.

events.title: Ghana leads the way
events.detail: The Gold Coast became Ghana in 1957, the first colony south of the Sahara to win independence. Guinea broke away from France a year later.

events.title: Egypt and Syria unite
events.detail: In 1958 Egypt and Syria merged as the United Arab Republic under Gamal Abdel Nasser, sharing one flag and one government in Cairo.

events.title: French Africa becomes independent
events.detail: In 1960 fourteen French colonies and trust territories became independent, from Senegal and Mauritania to Chad, Gabon and Madagascar.

events.title: The Congo gains independence
events.detail: Belgium’s vast colony became independent on 30 June 1960. Within weeks an army mutiny and the secession of Katanga had plunged it into crisis.

events.title: Nigeria and Somalia independent
events.detail: Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, became independent from Britain in October. In July, British and Italian Somaliland united as the Somali Republic.

eras.title: Decolonisation nears its end
eras.summary: Most colonies are now free and Vietnam is one country again, while the Iron Curtain still divides Europe and Germany.

events.title: Algeria wins independence
events.detail: After nearly eight years of war, Algeria became independent from France in July 1962, ending 132 years of French rule.

events.title: Britain leaves Africa
events.detail: From Sierra Leone in 1961 to the Seychelles in 1976, Britain’s African colonies became independent. In Rhodesia the white minority broke away alone in 1965.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.detail: In June 1967 Israel defeated Egypt, Jordan and Syria and occupied the West Bank, Gaza, the Sinai Peninsula and the Golan Heights.

events.title: Bangladesh is born
events.detail: East Pakistan, cut off from the west by India, won its independence in December 1971 after a nine-month war and became Bangladesh.

events.title: Britain leaves Arabia
events.detail: Britain left Kuwait in 1961 and Aden, now South Yemen, in 1967. In 1971 Bahrain and Qatar became independent and six sheikhdoms formed the United Arab Emirates.

events.title: Portugal leaves Africa
events.detail: After the 1974 revolution in Lisbon, Portugal let its African colonies go: Guinea-Bissau in 1974, then Mozambique, Cape Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe and Angola in 1975.

events.title: Vietnam is reunited
events.detail: The fall of Saigon in April 1975 ended the Vietnam War, and on 2 July 1976 North and South were joined as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

events.title: Western Sahara is divided
events.detail: Spain withdrew in February 1976. Morocco took the north and Mauritania the south, while the Polisario Front proclaimed a Sahrawi republic and fought both.

eras.title: Germany reunites
eras.summary: The Cold War is ending. Germany has reunited, Yemen has united and Namibia is independent, but the Soviet Union and Yugoslavia still stand.

events.title: Revolution in Iran
events.detail: The Islamic Revolution ended the Shah’s monarchy in 1979. The new Islamic Republic adopted its present flag the following year.

events.title: Zimbabwe is born
events.detail: After a long bush war and a brief return to British rule, Rhodesia became independent as Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980, under majority rule.

events.title: A last wave of independence
events.detail: From 1977 to 1984 Djibouti, Belize, Brunei, four Pacific island nations and five Caribbean island states left British or French rule.

events.title: Revolutions of 1989
events.detail: Communist rule collapsed across Eastern Europe. In Romania, crowds cut the socialist emblem out of the flag, leaving a hole at its centre.

events.title: Namibia’s independence
events.detail: After decades of South African rule and a long war, South West Africa became independent on 21 March 1990 as Namibia.

events.title: Yemen unites
events.detail: North Yemen and the socialist South joined on 22 May 1990 as the Republic of Yemen, with Sana’a as its capital.

events.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
events.detail: Iraqi forces overran Kuwait on 2 August 1990 and Baghdad declared it a province. The United Nations rejected the annexation and demanded a withdrawal.

events.title: Germany reunites
events.detail: Less than a year after the Berlin Wall fell, East Germany joined the Federal Republic on 3 October 1990. Berlin became one city again.

eras.title: After the Soviet Union
eras.summary: The Soviet Union and Yugoslavia have broken into new states, Czechoslovakia has split in two and Eritrea has just won independence.

events.title: Kuwait is liberated
events.detail: A US-led coalition drove Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in February 1991, ending a seven-month occupation and Iraq’s claimed annexation.

events.title: The Baltic states break free
events.detail: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania restored the independence they had lost in 1940. Moscow recognised them in September 1991.

events.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
events.detail: On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union was dissolved, leaving its twelve remaining republics, from Ukraine to Kazakhstan, as independent states.

events.title: Yugoslavia breaks apart
events.detail: Slovenia, Croatia and Macedonia declared independence in 1991, and Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992. War followed in Croatia and Bosnia.

events.title: A smaller Yugoslavia
events.detail: Serbia and Montenegro formed the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in April 1992, with a new tricolour flag.

events.title: Mujahideen take Kabul
events.detail: The communist government fell in April 1992 and an Islamic State of Afghanistan was proclaimed. Rival factions soon fought over the capital.

events.title: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully
events.detail: On 1 January 1993 Czechoslovakia divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, without a shot fired.

events.title: Eritrea becomes independent
events.detail: After thirty years of war and a referendum, Eritrea became independent on 24 May 1993. Ethiopia lost its whole coastline.

eras.title: South Sudan joins the map
eras.summary: Africa gains its newest state as South Sudan breaks away, while Kosovo and Montenegro finish the long unravelling of Yugoslavia.

events.title: Apartheid ends in South Africa
events.detail: After its first election open to all races in April 1994, with Nelson Mandela elected president, South Africa raised a new six-colour flag.

events.title: Hong Kong and Macau handed over
events.detail: Britain returned Hong Kong to China in 1997 and Portugal handed over Macau in 1999. Both keep their own laws as special administrative regions.

events.title: Zaire becomes DR Congo
events.detail: Laurent-Désiré Kabila’s rebels drove Mobutu from power in May 1997 and restored the name Democratic Republic of the Congo.

events.title: East Timor becomes independent
events.detail: Indonesian rule ended after a 1999 vote and a period of UN administration, and East Timor became independent as Timor-Leste in May 2002.

events.title: Montenegro goes its own way
events.detail: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, renamed Serbia and Montenegro in 2003, came to an end when Montenegro voted for independence in May 2006.

events.title: Kosovo declares independence
events.detail: Under UN administration since the 1999 war, Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in February 2008. Serbia, Russia, China and others do not recognise it.

events.title: South Sudan becomes independent
events.detail: After decades of civil war and a referendum in January, South Sudan left Sudan on 9 July 2011, becoming Africa’s newest country.

events.title: Libya’s old flag returns
events.detail: During the 2011 uprising, rebels raised the red, black and green flag of 1951 in place of Gaddafi’s plain green one, and it became Libya’s flag again.

eras.title: The world today
eras.summary: Recognised borders have barely moved since 2011. The changes are in names and flags, from Czechia and Eswatini to Türkiye and Syria.

events.title: Malawi’s rising sun returns
events.detail: Malawi brought back its original 1964 flag, with a red rising sun on the black band, two years after it was swapped for a flag with a full white sun.

events.title: Czechia as the short name
events.detail: The Czech Republic registered Czechia as its official short name with the United Nations. The full name, Czech Republic, is still in use.

events.title: Mauritania’s new flag
events.detail: After a referendum, Mauritania added red bands to the top and bottom of its green flag, honouring those who gave their lives for independence.

events.title: Swaziland becomes Eswatini
events.detail: Marking 50 years of independence, King Mswati III renamed the country Eswatini, its name in the siSwati language.

events.title: Macedonia becomes North Macedonia
events.detail: The Prespa Agreement with Greece ended a long dispute over the name Macedonia. The country became the Republic of North Macedonia.

events.title: Turkey becomes Türkiye
events.detail: At Ankara’s request, the United Nations began using Türkiye, the country’s own name, in place of Turkey.

events.title: Kyrgyzstan’s sun rays
events.detail: Kyrgyzstan redrew the sun on its flag with straight rays instead of wavy ones. The 40 rays and the yurt crown at its centre remain.

events.title: Syria’s new flag
events.detail: After the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, Syria adopted the green, white and black independence flag with three red stars.
